title: How to Know What to Say After You Say "Hi"
coreMove: After hello, place one useful handle into the exchange and return one of their own words so the next sentence has somewhere to go.
sourcePressure: Conversation-continuation unit covering techniques 10 through 23: matching mood, giving easy hooks, using context and visible objects, richer introductions, repeated words, spotlighting, parroting, and encore prompts.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is clever small talk. The useful version is building conversational fuel from context, introductions, repeated words, and prompts.

hook: The hardest part is after hi
tryThisNow: Ask someone how their day is going
Repeat the last word they said

exampleSpecs.domain: a specialty cheese counter during a Saturday tasting line
exampleSpecs.audience: a new cheesemonger who panics after greeting shoppers
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the line keeps moving and a hesitant shopper buys something unfamiliar
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the shopper says she needs something not too barnyard, he slides the ash-rind sample forward and repeats not too barnyard as the handle for the next question
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a slate board dusted with crumbs from an ash-rind cheese

exampleSpecs.domain: a dog adoption meet-and-greet in a shelter yard
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer who knows the animals but not how to draw out visitors
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a cautious family learns enough to consider a shy older dog
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when the father mentions quiet mornings, the volunteer kneels beside the blanket and turns quiet mornings into the next question instead of listing traits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a frayed blue leash looped through the shelter yard fence

exampleSpecs.domain: a rare-book fair booth where a collector pauses at a travel atlas
exampleSpecs.audience: a bookseller who tends to lecture about provenance too early
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a browser becomes engaged before drifting to the next aisle
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he notices the collector touching the foldout map, offers one concrete hook about the pencil route, then asks what coastline caught her eye
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a foldout map held flat by two velvet weights

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood tool library orientation for first-time members
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator introducing strangers without making them recite biographies
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether new members talk to each other and return for the repair night
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: instead of names plus jobs, she introduces each person with the object they came to borrow and one practical reason, giving everyone an immediate hook
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pegboard with empty outlines where borrowed tools should hang

exampleSpecs.domain: a planetarium lobby after a meteor-shower lecture
exampleSpecs.audience: a shy docent trying to keep visitors talking after the lights come up
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether visitors ask follow-up questions or leave with unanswered confusion
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she hears a teenager repeat the word radiant, points to the lobby star chart, and predicts the next question will be about where to look tonight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glowing star chart mounted beside the exit doors

exampleSpecs.domain: a winter farmers market booth selling seed packets to apartment gardeners
exampleSpecs.audience: a grower who needs to help novices without drowning them in details
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a first-time gardener leaves with a feasible plan instead of embarrassment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when the shopper says tiny balcony twice, the grower picks up the compact basil packet and uses tiny balcony as the doorway to narrow choices
exampleSpecs.firstImage: seed packets clipped to twine with miniature clothespins

skillTargets: select the best conversational handle from visible context
turn repeated words into natural expansion prompts
compare rich introductions with flat name-and-title introductions
diagnose when a question gives no easy material to answer

tryThisNowSpec: In your next casual exchange, listen for one repeated or vivid word, say that word back lightly, and add one concrete question that lets the person expand from it.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
